body: TL;DR ESPN streaming plans and bundles are increasing in price. Plans are increasing by $1 to $3 per month. Adjustments also affect many streaming bundles that include ESPN. As we’ve learned from 9to5Mac , ESPN has announced price hikes for its ESPN Select and ESPN Unlimited streaming plans. Select is increasing from $13 to $14 per month (or $140 per year, up from $130), while Unlimited is jumping from $30 to $32 per month (or $320 per year, from $300). Bundles including ESPN along with Disney Plus and Hulu are going up, too.

title: The Longest-Leading Billboard Hot 100 No. 1s
summary: A select few hits have led the chart for at least 10 weeks.
body: Beginning with Debby Boone’s “You Light Up My Life” in 1977, a relatively select few smashes have led the Billboard Hot 100 for at least 10 weeks. How few? Just a mere 4% of all Hot 100 No. 1s dating to the chart’s launch on Aug. 4, 1958, have earned the achievement. Olivia Newton-John’s “Physical” flexed 10 weeks at No. 1 in 1981-82, and that smash and Boone’s shared the mark for the longest Hot 100 reign for more than a decade, until Boyz II Men’s “End of the Road” dominated for 13 weeks in 1992. That best lasted briefly, as Whitney Houston’s “I Will Always Love You” led for 14 weeks in late 1992/early 1993. In 1995-96, Mariah Carey and Boyz II Men’s “One Sweet Day” ran up 16 weeks at No. 1, a milestone that held for more than 23 years. (Songs began logging longer No. 1 stays after the Hot 100 adopted electronically tracked data, according to Luminate, in late 1991.) In 2017, Luis Fonsi and Daddy Yankee’s “Despacito,” featuring Justin Bieber, tied the No. 1 run of “One Sweet Day.” By 2019, Lil Nas X’s “Old Town Road,” featuring Billy Ray Cyrus, collected 19 weeks atop the Hot 100, a mark matched by Shaboozey’s “A Bar Song (Tipsy)” beginning in July 2024 and — as of the Aug. 29, …

title: YouTube is bringing lots more content types to 24/7 Stations feeds

body: TL;DR YouTube introduced Stations earlier this year, featuring 24/7 content streams from musical artists. Now Google is expanding Stations to also include podcasts, creator content, and more. Access is only getting started with a small number of creators initially. Like any good streaming service, YouTube is always working to find the next big hook that will keep viewers glued to their screens, video after video. Earlier this year, we spotted a fresh addition to YouTube’s offerings in the form of Stations , 24/7 streams that appeared designed to connect you with an endless feed of content from your favorite musical artists. And now, Stations are getting a bit of an expansion. YouTube is constantly trying out new experiments, and this month, the service shares that its latest involves building Stations around even more diverse content than just music. While you’ll still see Stations from musical performers, they’re also starting to expand to cover podcasts, media channels, and just regular creator content.

The missing interface elements wouldn’t come back even after switching videos, restarting the iPad, or reinstalling the app.

title: Philips Hue is working on a more affordable TV sync box
summary: It's apparently a lot less expensive, but it won't do as much.
body: TL;DR A UK retailer has listed the unannounced Philips Hue Play Sync Box Lite. The new version offers only a single HDMI input, among other compromises. The Lite model is listed at retailer Very for £109.99 compared to the existing premium model’s £299.99. The Philips Hue Play HDMI sync box 8K lets you synchronize your smart lights with what’s happening on your TV to create a “fully immersive light syncing experience” (as Hue puts it), matching the color and brightness of your smart lights with your video content in real time. It’s cool, but it’s also wildly expensive at an MSRP of $385. Now, though, it looks like Philips Hue is set to release a new, stripped-back version at a more affordable price. As spotted by Hueblog , UK retailer Very has published a listing for an unannounced sync box from Philips, the Hue Play Sync Box Lite. The Lite version is shown as having one HDMI input (to the current model’s four), meaning you’ll be limited to syncing lights with a single device’s video. It’ll apparently be much less expensive, though: the Hue Play Sync Box Lite is listed at £109.99, about a third the price of the 8K model’s £299.99 UK MSRP.

body: المدرب الإسباني يرفع شعار "لا أحد فوق سان جيرمان" قرر لويس إنريكي مدرب باريس سان جيرمان، معاقبة أحد نجومه، قبل مباراة فريقه أمام رين، مساء أمس الأحد، في الجولة الأولى من الدوري الفرنسي. وكان سان جيرمان متأخرًا بهدفين دون رد، قبل أن يشارك الوافد الجديد فيران توريس مطلع الشوط الثاني، ويسجل هدفين لينتزع تعادلًا ثمينًا للفريق الباريسي. وأثبت إنريكي أنه لا أحد فوق الفريق، خلال مباراة رين ، بعدما استبدل النجمين عثمان ديمبلي وخفيتشا كفاراتسيخليا بين الشوطين، لينجح في النهاية في خطف نقطة. يمكنكم مناقشة الموضوعات والأخبار بشكل أعمق في منتديات كووورة لكن قائمة إنريكي لهذه المباراة أثارت جدلًا واسعًا، بعدما قرر المدير الفني الإسباني استبعاد اللاعب الشاب سيني مايولو. كان غياب مايولو ملحوظًا، فاللاعب البالغ من العمر 20 عامًا، الذي شارك في مباراتي لانس (السوبر الفرنسي) وأستون فيلا (السوبر الأوروبي)، لم يكن مصابًا ولا مريضًا. ووفقًا لشبكة " فوت ميركاتو " نقلًا عن صحيفة "ليكيب"، فقد دفع مايولو ثمن أسبوع من التدريبات التي اعتُبرت أقل جودة من تدريبات زملائه.

title: YouTube’s latest UI change improves how you get to a video’s juicy bits
summary: The update adds a visual timeline indicator when double-tapping to skip.
body: TL;DR YouTube may be rolling out a new seek UI on Android that shows how much time you’ve skipped through a video. The change appears on the stable YouTube app, but it hasn’t reached every device. The new behavior could be part of a broader YouTube UI refresh. YouTube’s interface has become something of a moving target lately. The company was only recently testing a new button arrangement on Android that removed text labels from the controls under videos. And now, a small change to how YouTube shows skipped time appears to be rolling out to some Android users. The change involves YouTube’s familiar double-tap gesture for skipping. Currently, you can double-tap the right side of the screen to jump forward or the left side to rewind, while touching and holding the scrub bar lets you manually move through the video. In the current UI, double-tapping skips forward or backward without showing how much time you’ve moved. When manually scrubbing, however, YouTube displays the amount of time you’ve skipped in the video interface, as seen in the screenshot below.

title: Now Playing on Pixel may be getting its big missing feature back
summary: Google could bring back Now Playing notifications after breaking them with a recent update.
body: Credit: Joe Maring / Android Authority TL;DR Google updated the Now Playing app on Pixel earlier this year — and removed the option to show notifications. It may now be working to bring notifications back. Google also appears to be working to add support for multiple users, which isn’t supported yet. Now Playing remains one of the most compelling reasons to buy a Pixel still . In March this year, Google brought a major update to Now Playing, advancing it with its own dedicated app . But the update also brought a few feature cutbacks and challenges, such as removing notifications about tracks being played in your surroundings. This broke popular use cases for using Now Playing’s notifications to import songs into apps, such as Last.fm. What followed was dissatisfaction from users, which Google is now looking to address. It is working to add notifications for the currently playing track back to the app with a future update.

title: The Google Play Store is working on a new way to find apps using images
summary: Code in the latest Play Store update reveals image attachments could soon be coming to Ask Play AI search.
body: Credit: Adamya Sharma / Android Authority TL;DR Google Play Store v52.8.55-34 code shows Ask Play will soon support direct image attachments from the phone’s camera or gallery. Users can upload screenshots to identify home screen widgets, features, specific types of apps, and more. Google may also retire the “Ask Play about this app” section in favor of sticky, horizontally scrollable question chips. At Google I/O 2026, Google unveiled an updated Ask Play conversational search feature within the Google Play Store. This feature was designed to help users discover apps and get high-level summaries through natural conversation and follow-up questions. Now, Google is preparing to make discovery even easier by allowing users to attach images directly to their Ask Play queries, alongside potentially sunsetting the “Ask Play about this app” section. title: Chrome’s new rules ruined ad blockers. Here are 4 things that still work
summary: You can still block ads — just not how you used to.
body: Credit: Edgar Cervantes / Android Authority A few years ago, Chrome introduced Manifest V3 and began phasing out the older Manifest V2 technology used by some of the most advanced browser extensions. According to Google, the older version was harder to maintain and had its own real security risks, but we suspect it’s also because Google wanted to rein in extension capabilities. Unfortunately, this also made it harder to install extensions like the highly popular uBlock Origin. While workarounds still existed by using Chrome flags, that’s no longer the case . It is now virtually impossible to get MV2 extensions to work in Chrome.

title: Galaxy S26 Ultra’s portrait lighting trick could be coming to the S25 Ultra
summary: The feature could help brighten subjects in uneven lighting.
body: TL;DR A leaked One UI 9 build shows the Galaxy S25 Ultra testing a tool that brightens backlit subjects without blowing out the background. The feature, Virtual Reflector, debuted on the Galaxy S26 Ultra and simulates a physical photography reflector in software. Samsung hasn’t confirmed a One UI 9 beta for the S25 series yet, so the feature could still be changed or dropped before release. Samsung appears to be preparing more than a routine software update for the Galaxy S25 series. Recent One UI 9 internal builds have already revealed camera features such as Horizontal Lock and My FanCam , and now another Galaxy S26 Ultra feature has surfaced on the Galaxy S25 Ultra. This time, Samsung could be giving its 2025 flagship a useful new tool to help with portraits in tricky lighting. Leaker Fahad Ali Javed shared screenshots on X showing the Virtual Reflector tool running on a Galaxy S25 Ultra with an internal One UI 9 build ending in ZZHC. SamMobile has also reported on the discovery, noting that Samsung is testing the feature through its Expert RAW camera app.

title: Google, take note: This phone maker’s new chipset looks like an absolute beast
summary: It even has an unannounced GPU.
body: TL;DR Xiaomi has announced the XRing 03 smartphone chipset. This chipset has an unannounced Arm G2-Ultra NX GPU and a 10-core CPU with no little cores. The chip will debut in the Xiaomi 18 Fold, which is scheduled to launch next month. Google has just launched the Pixel 11 series , and our own benchmarks show that the Tensor G6 chip is a significant step down from rival chips. Now, Xiaomi has revealed its XRing 03 processor, and it seemingly obliterates Google’s silicon on paper. Xiaomi revealed XRing 03 details on Weibo , and it packs a 3nm design from an unspecified foundry. However, what’s particularly interesting is that it comes with an unannounced Arm G2-Ultra NX GPU. Expect 16 cores, eight NX neural accelerators, and AI-based super-resolution/frame interpolation. In fact, Xiaomi claims that this GPU is 85% faster than last year’s XRing 01 , 64% more efficient, and 182% faster at ray tracing. For what it’s worth, the XRing 01 had an Immortalis G925 MC16 GPU. Either way, this seems far more impressive than the Tensor G6’s PowerVR CXTP-48-1536 GPU.

title: Google fixed this Google Maps issue on mobile, but it’s back now on Android Auto

body: TL;DR Traffic lines are disappearing from Google Maps on Android Auto for some users. The issue appears limited to Android Auto, not Maps on phones. Some users say the problem started after the Immersive Navigation update arrived. Google Maps users really can’t seem to catch a break lately. Not long after Google fixed a bug that made color-coded traffic lines disappear across Android, iOS, and desktop, the same issue has now appeared in Android Auto. Several users in the Android Auto community and on Reddit are reporting that Google Maps no longer shows the familiar green, yellow, orange, and red traffic lines on their car’s screen. The problem appears to be limited to Android Auto, with affected users reporting that traffic displays normally when they open Google Maps directly on their phones.

title: Nintendo just went nuclear on Switch emulators (again)
summary: Nintendo just can't stand Switch games running on anything other than a Switch.
body: TL;DR Nintendo has filed seven new DMCA notices taking down over 400 GitHub repositories related to Switch emulators. The notice took down repos for emulators such as Suyu, Skyline, and several others. It’s no secret that Nintendo has historically taken an extremely strict stance against emulators and people using its IP without permission. A few months ago, the company sent DMCA notices to take down several Switch emulators whose code was hosted on GitHub. Now, the company has thrown another proverbial Donkey Kong barrel at more such GitHub repositories. Nintendo has filed seven DMCA complaints with GitHub to take down over 400 repositories related to Switch emulators in a single day (via TorrentFreak ). This includes emulators like Suyu, which gained popularity after the Yuzu emulator shut down in 2024. According to the DMCA notice displayed publicly on the Suyu repository, GitHub took down all 311 repositories in the network due to Nintendo’s DMCA notice.

title: Pixel 11 Pro Fold cracks in bend test despite Google’s ‘3x stronger’ claims
summary: This makes the Pixel 11 Pro Fold the fourth consecutive Google foldable to fail in this aspect.
body: Credit: Joe Maring / Android Authority TL;DR The Google Pixel 11 Pro Fold has failed JerryRigEverything’s popular bend test. The phone cracked along both antenna lines next to the hinge, and its outer display also popped right off during the test. Google has touted a redesigned build that is three times stronger, but it looks like the same antenna-line area is still the phone’s weakest point, and the battery placement is also not ideal. Google’s Pixel 11 Pro Fold has failed JerryRigEverything’s popular durability test for a second year in a row. After the Pixel 10 Pro XL literally exploded during the same durability test last year, it looks like Google still hasn’t improved the Pixel 11 Pro’s weakest structural point.
